That figure is the Sobol share of the CPU pipeline (F04: 2.6% at 8x52, 1.8% at 4x12), not of the GPU end-to-end time. The relevant test is whether 4 feeders plus inter-process transfer keep up with the device (about 1.4e6 Sobol points/s from 4 feeders vs about 2.6e5 kernel points/s at 8x52, but about 0.9 GB/s of float64 uniforms through Windows IPC, whose mechanism is not pinned). Original minor. C2 'Scope: development cases; knock-out payoff'; C8 '1 warm timing repeat to 2^17, fitted on marks 2^13...2^17'. Choosing 2^17 over F18's 2^19 matches C8's C1 depth; acceptable.

The section 0.3 minimum includes the plain-MC anchors 'converted with N = (t*sigma_plain/0.45eps)^2'. t and sigma_plain are undefined. The conversion divides N by a throughput from 10-second launches, so it has no setup, launch, transfer or reduction time and no accuracy check. Every other candidate includes these ('Every wall time runs from task submission ... including per-run setup') and carries at least one 2^12-point chunk. With P1 sigma and the F03/F17 throughputs, the GPU anchor gives about 8 ms (4x12) and 27 ms (8x52) at $0.10 and 0.09 s / 0.30 s at $0.03. The RQMC candidates cost at least about 0.08 s / 0.66 s for the first chunk. The anchor therefore sets T_C at the two largest eps by a protocol difference. This is classical-favourable for the frontier (claim C6) and is not labelled. 'Validated' is also undefined for the anchors and for item C1 rqmc (only preint has a port check). 'item C5's best method if it is faster on CPU' does not say at which eps.
fix: Define t = z_{.995} and sigma_plain = the section 0.4 sigma_Q. Time each anchor end-to-end at its N (or add a measured fixed cost from a timed small-N launch plus reduction), and label any throughput-only row CF. Validate anchors and rqmc by the C3-style agreement test against the C4 reference at a stated N. State the C6 porting criterion (e.g. lower primary CPU T_C($0.001)).

detail: Nothing fixes which execution is primary if an item is re-run after a crash, a code fix or any other change. 'Runners refuse to overwrite an existing output directory' only stops silent overwrites; a re-run into a new directory is unconstrained. 'Committed Stage C code may be added after this file' lets timing-bearing code (P3b, CUDA kernel, feeders) change after C2 timings are seen. 'this file itself is not edited after the first run' allows edits between the freezing commit and the first run. Timing enters D_max linearly, so this is the main remaining post-hoc lever.
fix: Add: 'The first complete execution of each item from a committed revision is primary. A re-execution is allowed only for a crash, a failed validation or a test-detected defect, is logged with its reason in the deviation log before it starts, and every completed execution is reported. Timing-bearing code is fixed at a recorded commit before the item's first timing run. This file is not edited after its freezing commit except for the appended deviation log.'

ref: C4 primary check vs C2 measured confirmation
detail: If under-coverage is declared, 'n(eps) is recomputed with c ... that T_C is primary'. But T_C comes from the C2 measured confirmation, which has already run on Day 1 at the t-based n_run, and C2 says 'n is never re-chosen'. The spec does not say whether the new T_C comes from a fresh confirmation at the new n_run, from scaling the measured time by (c/t_{.995,15})^{1/r}, or from the all-16 model. Nor does it say whether c (estimated for preint only) applies to rqmc, the C5 methods, the GPU kernels and the anchors in the section 0.3 minimum, or to items C7/C8. Each option gives a different primary T_C, chosen after the coverage result is known.
fix: Fix one rule now, e.g. 'every RQMC candidate's primary T_C at that case is multiplied by (c/t_{.995,15})^{1/r} with its own r, with no re-run; the anchors are unchanged; items C7/C8 are unchanged and the paper states their coverage is assumed.'

detail: If the Ref A/Ref B test fails, 'item C4 is run against each reference separately'. Several things are then undefined: which reference decides the primary under-coverage check, what 'the item C4 reference' means in C5 unbiasedness and in the secondary P1/P3/P3b tests, and what is reported as the paper's price. The analyst would choose after seeing both coverages.
fix: Add: 'On failure, the under-coverage check uses the reference giving the lower coverage (QF); C5 unbiasedness passes only if it passes against both; secondary tests are reported against both; the paper reports both prices and no combined reference.'

ref: 0.2 basis rows; 0.4 e_C row; decision-point sensitivity rows
detail: The QF/CF basis rows rank bases by T_C($0.001), and the e_C = 0.9eps row needs T_C at a new n(eps). Measured confirmation exists only for the canonical factor at the primary n_run, and the C5/C6 candidates have no basis variants. The T_C computation for these rows is undefined (measured vs modelled, and how the section 0.3 minimum is formed). The canonical row is measured while the others can only be modelled, which biases the ranking.
fix: State: 'Basis and e_C rows use the all-16 warm model a + b*n at that row's n(eps) for each C1 method; candidates without basis variants keep their canonical primary T_C; the canonical row is also shown on the model convention for comparison.'

detail: (a) C8's counts and 'Any case <= 10 ... re-plan trigger' do not say which of depths (a) favourable score or (b) compiled is used. (b) C8 does not state its T_C convention (C7 states all-16). (c) The development cases have no stated consequence if the decision-point ratio falls to <= 10, although they now get a new comparator. (d) The decision-point table says it uses 'the section 0.3 comparator' for the item C7 cases, while C7 says T_C is 'preint CPU only'.

detail: No collision found among the declared keys. Note that numpy SeedSequence zero-pads entropy to 4 words (verified in T0: [a,b,c] == [a,b,c,0]; [a,b,c,0] != [a,b,c,0,0]), so 3- and 4-word keys can alias. Gaps: 'eps_index' undefined; sigma_Q 'root of the item' undefined for development cases; Ref A's purpose code unstated; Q4 uses purpose 5, which is not in the purpose list, plus '...'; no seeds for Q4's two 10^7-path runs; replication indices of the 4x12 2^17 coverage arm and of the fresh-cached and cold repeats unstated; the bootstrap root 2026100112 is not in the roots list.
fix: Define eps_index (0 = $0.10 ... 3 = $0.001). Use the C1 root for development-case sigma_Q. Give Ref A purpose 2 with replication 1. Add purposes 5 (Q4 draws), 6 (Q4 10^7-path law and flip runs) and 8 (bootstrap). Write every key as 5 words.

ref: C1 pipeline vs C2 timing conventions
detail: C1 says 'The factor is built once per worker process', but C2 says every wall time includes 'per-run setup (factor, ...)'. These contradict for warm runs. How the 5 warm repeats become the primary model is unstated: a fit to per-mark medians or the median of per-repeat (a, b). Also unstated: whether the small-n 'measured warm all-16 elapsed time' is a median over repeats, how many repeats convention (iii) gets, and how n_run < 2^12 is handled (e.g. 8x52 at $0.01, n_run = 2^11) given 2^12 chunks.
fix: State: factor built per run inside the timed interval (or per worker and excluded, labelled CF). Primary model = OLS on the per-mark median over the 5 warm repeats. Small-n time = median over warm repeats. Convention (iii) gets 5 warm repeats. A run with n_run < 2^12 draws one chunk of n_run points.

detail: Several non-neutral choices are unlabelled, contrary to 'Every choice that is not neutral carries a label'. CF: taking the minimum over many noisy candidate T_C (selection bias toward lucky fits and timings); the rigorous row's quantum failure probability 0.003 instead of 0.01. QF: the one-sided pooled scaling (scaled up when hw16 > 0.45eps, never down); host-generated GPU uniforms as primary; float32 excluded above eps/10 while a quantum overrun only reduces e_Q; the C4-recalibrated T_C as primary; the C7 all-16 primary vs the median sensitivity. All label directions present in v2 were checked and are correct (e.g. warm CF, fresh-cached QF, n_run rounding QF, e_C = 0.9eps CF, unreduced Q4 share QF, favourable score QF).
fix: Add the listed labels in the tables, or one sentence per item stating its direction.

detail: (a) Law error 'upper 99% bound' of a signed difference: a negative difference gives a negative bound that would lower the total. (b) 'the analytic fixed-point bound if available' lets the analyst skip a computation that can only raise delta (QF lean). (c) '>= 10^4 per case; fewer is a recorded deviation' reopens the draw count with no permitted reason; F12 measured 10^4 B8x52 draws at about 12 min single-process. (d) The IR exposes only the payoff output; delta_fp per date needs basket nodes located by tracing back from the lt(max-basket, H) node (node 5644 in B4x12/target.json). This is feasible but not stated.
fix: Bound |law error| as max(|lower|, |upper|) of the 99% interval. Either compute the analytic bound or state that it is not used. Drop the 'fewer' clause. Define delta_fp on the comparator input max_j basket_j (traceable via ir.evaluate(trace=True)) if per-date nodes are not identified.

detail: (a) The primary coverage check does not say whether raw or widened coverage is used. (b) The Bonferroni level '1 - 0.05/16' counts 2 cases x 4 n x 2 levels, but the 4x12 2^17 arm adds 2 cells, making 18. (c) 'it counts as resolved only if the resolution is <= $10^-4': 'resolution' is undefined. As hw99(A) + hw99(B) it is about 2.4e-4 at 4x12 (never resolved). As the combined reference hw99 it is about 4e-5 (resolvable). The outcome depends on the reading.
fix: Primary check uses raw coverage. Use /18 or exclude the 2^17 arm from the family explicitly. Define resolution = hw99(A) + hw99(B) (the plan's agreement resolution).

detail: (a) The Day 1 overnight slot holds Ref B (12 h of the 16-process pool) plus Ref A (about 0.5 h) and item C4 (about 1.2 h including the 4x12 2^17 arm, about 45 min), so about 14 h. If run concurrently, Ref B's wall-clock budget buys fewer paths, so its precision depends on scheduling. (b) Exclusivity covers only 'other Stage C job[s]', but the spec itself says another session uses this machine. (c) 'load average' does not exist on Windows, and psutil is not in the T0 lock. (d) 'Every run size and prefix is a power of 2' contradicts Ref B's wall-clock stop and Q4's 5,000-draw sets.
fix: Run Ref B alone (or budget it in process-hours). Require no other compute job of any session during timing runs, checked by a stated Windows counter (e.g. typeperf processor time before and after). Scope the power-of-2 rule to Sobol runs.

detail: 'A cut is decided at the start of a day ... from elapsed time only' gives no numeric trigger. C8 can still be cut at the start of Day 3 after the C7 robustness outcomes are known, and nothing makes the reason checkable. The C6 cut ('carry g in {1, 10, 100}') does not say how g enters T_C or what happens to the plain-MC anchors, which belong to C6.
fix: Give a trigger, e.g. 'C8 is cut only if Day 3 starts later than calendar day X or fewer than N machine-hours remain before Day 5'. State that under the C6 cut, T_C/g rows are sensitivities and the CPU anchor stays in the minimum.

ref: 0.2 Development cases also run the archived factor
detail: Only the 8x52 archived single-thread factor exists ('L_8x52_numpy1.26.4_single_thread.npy'). The 4x12 file in q0_attribution ('eigh_4x12_numpy1.26.4.npz') comes from the diagnostic that imported numpy before pinning threads, i.e. multithreaded MKL. The 4x12 archived factor is therefore unspecified, and an analyst could pick either.
fix: State: 'For 4x12 the archived factor is the T0 single-thread eigh factor, which reproduced every archived 4x12 P3 field exactly (Q0); its hash is recorded.' Or regenerate it with numpy 1.26.4 and threads pinned, and record the hash.

detail: Sobol scrambles are seeded with 'np.random.default_rng([root, case.dim, scramble])'. The spec requires 'SeedSequence([root, case_index, purpose, replication, scramble])'. Case has no case_index, and there is no purpose or replication. Consequences: the four C8 cases of a stratum share identical Sobol points; C2 repeats, confirmations and C4 replications cannot get distinct keys; outputs cannot be replayed from the spec text.
fix: Add case_index to Case and (purpose, replication) to the task, and seed with qmc.Sobol(dim, scramble=True, seed=np.random.default_rng([root, case_index, purpose, replication, s])). Keep the P3 key only on the port-check path.

ref: scrambles.py factor(); test_basis.py rotation test; spec 0.2
detail: Rotations are seeded with '[rotation_root, case.dim, basis[1]]', not '[2026100101, case_index, q]'. The test uses '[2026100101, 852, 0]', which matches neither the code nor the spec. Spec q = 1..4; the code and tests use q = 0. Otherwise the recipe matches: one generator drawn in canonical eigenspace order, QR, 'q *= np.sign(np.diag(r))', L_E <- L_E Q.
fix: Seed with [2026100101, case.case_index, q], q in 1..4, and update the test to a spec key.

ref: scrambles.py run_scramble; spec C1 'built once per worker process'
detail: run_scramble calls factor() inside every task, so the factor is rebuilt per scramble, and for the 'eigh' basis LAPACK runs once per scramble (about 0.45 s at 8x52). Harmless for rates; wrong for C2 timing under the spec's pipeline and the source of the NS-08 ambiguity.
fix: Build the factor in a pool initializer (per worker, per case and basis), or make the per-run build explicit, to match whichever rule NS-08 fixes.

ref: scrambles.py; spec section 0 outputs and 0.2 archived factor
detail: There is no 'archived' basis option (load q0_attribution/L_8x52_numpy1.26.4_single_thread.npy with a hash check). Results record no SHA-256 of L, code, spec or lock, all of which section 0 requires in every JSON.
fix: Add an 'archived' basis that loads and hash-checks the .npy, and return sha256(L.tobytes()) in each task result.

detail: The spec asks that 'the 4x12 column order and its first two eigenspaces equal hard-coded values'. The test hard-codes the (asset, time) order of 10 columns and the group indices [[1,2,3],[6,7,8]]. It compares column directions with vectors rebuilt from the module's own asset_basis and the same sine formula, not with stored numbers. Helmert is checked independently against scipy.linalg.helmert. Consistent checks: lexsort((t_idx, a_idx, -lam)) as in 0.1; flattening asset*nt + date; time vectors and eigenvalues as in 0.1; L independent of BLAS threads (1 vs 22). All 20 tests in research/frontier_classical_20261001 pass in the T0 venv.
fix: Store a few numeric entries (e.g. L[:4, :9] for 4x12 to 1e-15) as literals.
